baselines: Naive/empty baseline: submission/vulnerability_report.json omits vulnerable_state or reports an incorrect state (e.g., IDLE), and mitigation is a generic non-redundant statement -- must FAIL all SR checks.
No existing benchmark found for this exact fault-injection-on-FSM-privilege-transition scenario; task is novel within side_channel_fault_analysis domain.

metrics.description: Whether the submission correctly identifies the exact vulnerable FSM state and resulting elevated privilege value caused by the instruction-skip fault, verified optionally via iverilog/vvp cross-simulation.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Fraction of FSM states in the transition_sequence for which the submission correctly reports the skip impact (matching ground-truth per-state outcomes, including correctly identifying non-impactful states).
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Quality and specificity of the proposed redundancy-based mitigation, scored by presence of genuine redundancy mechanisms (duplication/triplication/re-check) targeted at the correct vulnerable write, versus vague or irrelevant suggestions.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

metrics.description: Rate at which the submission incorrectly flags fault-tolerant (non-write) states as producing a changed privilege outcome under skip.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

acceptance_criteria: FAIL if vulnerable_state does not match the ground-truth write-bearing state.
FAIL if resulting_privilege does not equal 'supervisor' (or the correct high-privilege label used in design_brief.md) for the vulnerable_state entry.
FAIL if any non-vulnerable state's priv_reg_after_skip differs from fault_free_final_priv (false positive fault claim).
FAIL if mitigation lacks a redundancy mechanism (duplication/triplication/re-check-and-correct).
FAIL if per_state_skip_impact is missing entries for any state in transition_sequence or fault_free_final_priv is not '00'.
PASS requires all required JSON fields present with correct types AND all SR1-SR4 checks satisfied.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: Skipping the priv_reg write in state DEMOTE leaves priv_reg at its prior value 2'b10 (supervisor) instead of transitioning to 2'b00 (user), because DEMOTE is the sole state that performs the write during the demotion sequence; all other states in the sequence (IDLE, CHECK, SETTLE, DONE) do not write priv_reg so skipping their actions does not change the final privilege outcome. Mitigation: duplicate the demotion write (write priv_reg <= 2'b00 in both DEMOTE and SETTLE, or add a redundant check-and-rewrite in the state following DEMOTE that re-asserts priv_reg==2'b00 and forces it if not, e.g. a triplicated/duplicated write with a comparator that flags mismatch and re-executes the write) so a single skipped write cycle is corrected by the redundant write in the next cycle.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String/semantic match of 'vulnerable_state' against the ground-truth state name derived from mode_sequencer.v; cross-check via iverilog simulation forcing a skip of that state's write and comparing simulated priv_reg to the reported 'resulting_privilege'.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify DEMOTE (or the equivalently-named state in the shipped design that performs the sole priv_reg write during the demotion sequence) as the vulnerable_state whose skip leaves priv_reg at the supervisor value.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compare each non-vulnerable-state entry's priv_reg_after_skip to fault_free_final_priv; flag mismatches. Optionally cross-simulate each state's skip via iverivog/vvp testbench harness.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly report that skipping any non-write state (IDLE, CHECK, SETTLE, DONE or equivalents) does NOT alter the final priv_reg outcome, i.e. per_state_skip_impact entries for those states must equal fault_free_final_priv.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Keyword/semantic scoring of 'mitigation' field for redundancy concepts (duplicate, triplicate, re-check, comparator, re-write, voting) combined with reference to the correct vulnerable state or write signal; reject vague/generic answers.
security_requirements.requirement: The reported mitigation must be a genuine redundancy-based hardware countermeasure (e.g., duplicated write with comparator, triplicated write/voting, or re-assert-and-check in a subsequent state) rather than a generic or non-redundant suggestion (e.g., 'add more testing', 'use encryption').

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Cross-check via iverilog/vvp simulation of mode_sequencer.v with a forced skip at the reported vulnerable_state's write cycle; compare final priv_reg register value against resulting_privilege mapping (2'b10 -> supervisor).
security_requirements.requirement: The reported resulting_privilege for the vulnerable_state skip must match the actual simulated privilege level (supervisor), not merely a plausible-sounding guess.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker with physical or logical access capable of injecting a transient fault (voltage/clock glitch, EM pulse, or laser fault injection) at a single clock cycle can suppress the register-write side effect of one FSM state without disrupting state-sequencing logic. If this skip lands on the unique state responsible for lowering privilege during a supervisor-to-user demotion, the sequencer proceeds through the remaining states and asserts 'done' while priv_reg still holds the supervisor value, allowing subsequently executed code to run with elevated privilege it should not have.

constraints: mode_sequencer.v must be synthesizable Verilog-2001 compatible with iverilog, self-contained (no external module dependencies beyond standard primitives).

The demotion sequence must take at least 3 clock cycles with priv_reg written in exactly one intermediate state, and fault-free transitions (no fault injected) must always produce priv_reg=2'b00 (user) at completion.

design_brief.md must document the full state list, state encoding, and the exact cycle in which priv_reg is written during demotion, without naming any specific vulnerability, CWE, or security requirement.

fault_model.md must describe the generic single-step instruction-skip fault mechanism (a state's write action is suppressed but FSM advances normally) applicable to any state, without indicating which state is exploitable.
Participants must not edit any file under inputs/; only submission/vulnerability_report.json is graded.

functional_requirements.requirement: The report must list every FSM state involved in the demotion transition sequence (from req_demote assertion to done) in execution order, with the exact state names as documented in design_brief.md, under a JSON field 'transition_sequence' (array of strings).
The report must state the fault-free final value of priv_reg after a complete demotion sequence with no skipped step, as a 2-bit binary string, under field 'fault_free_final_priv' (e.g. '00').

The report must identify, for each state in the transition sequence, whether skipping that state's write action changes the final priv_reg value relative to fault_free_final_priv, reported as an array field 'per_state_skip_impact' where each entry has fields 'state' (string) and 'priv_reg_after_skip' (2-bit binary string).

The report JSON must validate against the schema in response_format: all required top-level fields present with correct types, and 'per_state_skip_impact' must contain one entry for every state listed in 'transition_sequence'.

public_spec.interface: Module under analysis: mode_sequencer.v, module name mode_sequencer, ports: input clk, input rst_n (active-low async reset), input req_demote (public control input requesting a privilege lowering sequence), input req_promote (public control input requesting privilege raise), output reg [1:0] priv_reg (2'b10=supervisor/high, 2'b00=user/low, 2'b01/2'b11 reserved), output reg [3:0] state (current FSM state code, Moore-encoded, one-hot or binary as implemented, values documented in design_brief.md), output done (asserted for exactly one cycle when the current transition sequence completes). The sequencer transitions through a fixed sequence of named states (IDLE, CHECK, DEMOTE, SETTLE, DONE for a demotion request) over multiple clock cycles, writing priv_reg in a specific state during that sequence. The fault model (fault_model.md) defines a single-step instruction skip: on a designated fault cycle, the state-defined register-write action for exactly one state is suppressed (the FSM still advances to the next state, but the write it would have performed does not occur). The submission is a JSON answer file at submission/vulnerability_report.json (schema given in response_format) that must not modify mode_sequencer.v or any input artifact; evaluate.py reads inputs/ for reference and may optionally invoke iverilog/vvp to simulate mode_sequencer.v with a forced single-step skip at the state the submission names, cross-checking the reported resulting privilege value against the simulated trace.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided RTL control sequencer (mode_sequencer.v) which manages a privilege register through a documented multi-state transition sequence. Determine the behavior of the state machine under a fault model where a single control step (one FSM state's register-write action) can be skipped due to a transient glitch, and produce a vulnerability report describing which skipped step alters the final privilege outcome, what privilege state results, and a concrete redundancy-based mitigation for the affected step. Fault-free operation of the sequencer must remain fully documented and correct in your report.
public_spec.response_format: submission/vulnerability_report.json must be a single JSON object with required fields: 'transition_sequence' (array of strings, state names in order), 'fault_free_final_priv' (string, 2-bit binary), 'per_state_skip_impact' (array of objects each with 'state':string and 'priv_reg_after_skip':string 2-bit binary), 'vulnerable_state' (string, the single state whose skip leaves privilege elevated), 'resulting_privilege' (string, e.g. 'supervisor' or 'user'), and 'mitigation' (string, a concrete redundancy-based hardware mitigation description, e.g. duplicate-write-and-check). No other top-level fields are required but extras are ignored.

title: Instruction-skip fault at a privilege-mode transition
